tagline: Thirteen miles of Route 66 that the interstate passed by.
intro: Route 66 comes over from Missouri on State Line Road and turns into Galena by Front and Main streets, then runs west on K-66 to Riverton and on to the concrete arch over Brush Creek before heading south through Baxter Springs to the Oklahoma line. It is about 13 miles end to end, all of it in Cherokee County, in old lead and zinc mining country.
Kansas paved its stretch in 1929, the first state to do so. When Interstate 44 came through in 1961 it crossed straight from Oklahoma into Missouri and missed Kansas by a quarter of a mile.

moments.title: Galena
moments.text: Lead found in 1877 named the town and once filled it with over 30,000 people, and a restored Kan-O-Tex station now keeps the original boom truck from the Mater story.

moments.title: Riverton
moments.text: Pixar's researchers stopped at the Eisler Brothers store here and met Dean Walker, who could turn his feet backwards and walk in reverse, one of the models for Mater.

moments.title: Rainbow Bridge
moments.text: Built over Brush Creek in 1923, the last Marsh arch left on all of old 66 still takes cars on a short one-way spur beside its replacement.

sources.label: Kansas Tourism, Kansas Historic Route 66 Byway
